sourceTitle: Why Different Currencies Have Different Values
title: A Strong Currency Doesn't Mean A Strong Economy
hook: A strong currency does not mean a strong economy.
question: Which would you rather hold?

scenes.narration: People think a strong currency means a strong economy. It does not.
A currency's value is just a price, set by supply, demand, and trust. Japan keeps its yen weak on purpose, to sell more exports.
scenes.line: It's a price, not a scoreboard

scenes.narration: The dollar is in eighty-eight percent of all currency trades on Earth. Not because America is flawless, but because the world trusts it.
scenes.label: involve the US dollar

scenes.narration: And a big number means nothing by itself. One Zimbabwean banknote once read one hundred trillion dollars, and bought almost nothing.
scenes.label: Zimbabwe dollars — nearly worthless

scenes.narration: So which would you actually rather hold?
